literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) describe a 3xHA epitope tag inserted after the signal peptide of ACE2 (Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, UniProt Q9BYF1, gene ACE2), not ACE (Angiotensin-converting enzyme 1, UniProt P12821, gene ACE). ACE and ACE2 are human paralogs — both encoded in the human genome by different genes — not orthologs. The rules permit evidence from 'a close ortholog' (same gene in a different species), which ACE2 is not. No ledger line reports a tolerated tag insertion in ACE itself or in a genuine ortholog of ACE (e.g., mouse Ace). Accordingly, no site is grounded in the ledger and the site list is empty. For completeness: ACE (P12821) is a type-I transmembrane protein with signal peptide 1–29, a large extracellular domain 30–1259, TM 1260–1277, and a short cytoplasmic tail 1278–1306. The mature N-terminus (residue 30, L) is extracellular and would be the topologically analogous position to the ACE2 site described in L1–L6, but without a qualifying ledger line for ACE, no site can be proposed.
